verification.summary: The duplicate/cap-check awk block relies on gawk's 3-arg match(s,r,arr) extension, which errors out under plain POSIX awk/mawk (common default on Debian/Ubuntu), so the whole duplicate-detection guard can silently break the script. Several JSON reads use whitespace-sensitive grep patterns instead of a JSON parser, so they'll break the moment the service pretty-prints output, which the contract never rules out.

mustFix.problem: match() with a third capture-array argument is a gawk extension, not POSIX awk. If the box's default `awk` is mawk/one-true-awk (very common on Debian/Ubuntu), this line throws a syntax/runtime error and check_snapshots never runs the dup check it exists for, which is the one thing accs.md says must terminate with an error if violated.

Nothing in the contract guarantees compact, no-space JSON, so a serializer that emits '"id": 5' (space after colon) or pretty-printed output breaks every grep-based extraction (COUNT1, COUNT2, FIRST_ID) in the script even when the implementation is correct, stalling the dev agent on a false failure.

shouldFix.problem: This line computes a value that's never read afterward (the real check is the python3 block below it) — dead code that just adds noise and a second fragile grep pattern for no benefit.

shouldKnow.problem: Truncation/'...' behavior from the contract is never exercised since the cap is forced to 500 for the whole run — correct per accs.md's instruction to size the buffer to fit everything, but worth knowing the default-cap and truncation table in the enriched spec stay unverified by this ACCS.
